Ui.Script:
-- ── The pool ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- One screen line per pool string, and the list of the ones currently in flight. The pool -- is fixed: a message arriving with all twenty busy evicts the oldest. NUM_COMBAT_TEXT_LINES = 20 COMBAT_TEXT_TO_ANIMATE = {}
-- ── Where a line sits ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS is the seat and the target the current float mode implies; it is -- filled in by CombatText_UpdateDisplayedMessages, not here. A new line is pushed clear of -- everything already in flight by one line plus COMBAT_TEXT_SPACING, but the stack never -- runs further than COMBAT_TEXT_MAX_OFFSET from the seat — past that it starts over. The -- staggered types jitter sideways by up to half COMBAT_TEXT_STAGGER_RANGE either way, so a -- flurry of hits does not print as one column. COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS = {} COMBAT_TEXT_SPACING = 10 COMBAT_TEXT_MAX_OFFSET = 130 COMBAT_TEXT_STAGGER_RANGE = 20
-- ── How long a line lives ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- It travels for COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLLSPEED seconds; COMBAT_TEXT_FADEOUT_TIME is when the -- fade STARTS, not how long it takes, so the fade is the tail of the same window. COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLLSPEED = 1.9 COMBAT_TEXT_FADEOUT_TIME = 1.3
-- ── How big it is drawn ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- An ordinary line is COMBAT_TEXT_HEIGHT and stays there. A crit "pops": seeded at the -- minimum, grown to the maximum across CRIT_SCALE_TIME, and back down to ordinary size by -- CRIT_SHRINKTIME (CombatText_OnUpdate walks that envelope). COMBAT_TEXT_HEIGHT = 25 COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_MINHEIGHT = 30 COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_MAXHEIGHT = 60 COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_SCALE_TIME = 0.05 COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_SHRINKTIME = 0.2
-- ── When the low-resource warnings latch ──────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Fractions of the bar, tested on the way down; see CombatText_LowResourceWarning. COMBAT_TEXT_LOW_HEALTH_THRESHOLD = 0.2 COMBAT_TEXT_LOW_MANA_THRESHOLD = 0.2
-- The option family: every saved global this feature owns, next to the value it ships -- with. **All fourteen are the spec's own defaults** (UIOptionsFrame.lua l.69-84), the -- master SHOW_COMBAT_TEXT included — it shipped "1" against the spec's "0" from 0578 to -- 1804 (see the header). Held to that by -- `reference_ui::tests::our_saved_ui_globals_default_to_the_references_own_values`, which -- reads the reference's file off the player's chain rather than trusting this comment. -- -- Each name is assigned AT FILE SCOPE and registered for saving in the same pass, because -- the load order is what makes a saved value stick (decision 1128): defaults first, the -- saved chunk over the top, consumers third; reverse any two and a saved value can never -- win. The Options window's Combat page drives all fourteen (decision 1134) and takes its -- "Defaults" from these very globals, read at each row's OnLoad — which runs before the -- saved chunk — so a default lives in exactly one place, this table, and the panel cannot -- drift from it. local combatTextOptions = { {"SHOW_COMBAT_TEXT", "0"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_LOW_HEALTH_MANA", "1"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_AURAS", "1"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_AURA_FADE", "0"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_COMBAT_STATE", "1"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_DODGE_PARRY_MISS", "0"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_RESISTANCES", "0"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_REPUTATION", "0"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_REACTIVES", "0"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_FRIENDLY_NAMES", "0"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_COMBO_POINTS", "0"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_MANA", "0"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_HONOR_GAINED", "1"}, {"COMBAT_TEXT_FLOAT_MODE", "1"}, } for i = 1, getn(combatTextOptions) do local name, default = combatTextOptions[i][1], combatTextOptions[i][2] setglobal(name, default) RegisterForSave(name) end
-- The message words (shipped enUS GlobalStrings values, hardcoded like the rest of our -- enUS-only data; or-guarded so an earlier definition wins). MANA = MANA or "Mana" RAGE = RAGE or "Rage" FOCUS = FOCUS or "Focus" ENERGY = ENERGY or "Energy" HEALTH_LOW = HEALTH_LOW or "Health Low" MANA_LOW = MANA_LOW or "Mana Low" ENTERING_COMBAT = ENTERING_COMBAT or "Entering Combat" LEAVING_COMBAT = LEAVING_COMBAT or "Leaving Combat" BLOCK = BLOCK or "Block" ABSORB = ABSORB or "Absorb" RESIST = RESIST or "Resist" SPELL_MISSED = SPELL_MISSED or "Miss" SPELL_DODGED = SPELL_DODGED or "Dodge" SPELL_PARRIED = SPELL_PARRIED or "Parry" SPELL_BLOCKED = SPELL_BLOCKED or "Block" SPELL_EVADED = SPELL_EVADED or "Evade" SPELL_IMMUNE = SPELL_IMMUNE or "Immune" SPELL_DEFLECTED = SPELL_DEFLECTED or "Deflect" SPELL_REFLECTED = SPELL_REFLECTED or "Reflect" SPELL_RESISTED = SPELL_RESISTED or "Resist" SPELL_ABSORBED = SPELL_ABSORBED or "Absorb" AURA_END = AURA_END or "<%s> fades" BLOCK_TRAILER = BLOCK_TRAILER or " (%d blocked)" ABSORB_TRAILER = ABSORB_TRAILER or " (%d absorbed)" RESIST_TRAILER = RESIST_TRAILER or " (%d resisted)" COMBAT_TEXT_HONOR_GAINED = COMBAT_TEXT_HONOR_GAINED or "Honor %s"
--[[ COMBAT_TEXT_TYPE_INFO — one entry per message type, and the four things an entry says:
r, g, b the colour the line prints in, as 0..1 floats show 1 while this type is currently being printed, nil while it is not. CombatText_UpdateDisplayedMessages rewrites it for every gated type from the option `var` names, so an entry carrying `var` and no `show` has merely not been refreshed yet, while an entry carrying `show` and no `var` is on for as long as the feature itself is isStaggered 1 to jitter the line sideways instead of printing it on the centre line var the name of the saved global that gates this type; nil = ungated
This table is API: addons index it by message-type key and read and write these fields, so the keys and the values are exactly the specification's. The rows below are OURS — almost every type shares its colour and its gate with several others, so the facts are written once per group and the loop underneath expands them into one entry per type. Fresh table per entry, never a shared one: `show` is rewritten per entry, and an addon may edit any single entry without that leaking into its neighbours. ]]
-- The six colours the whole table draws from. local CT_WHITE = {1, 1, 1} local CT_RED = {1, 0.1, 0.1} local CT_GREEN = {0.1, 1, 0.1} local CT_BLUE = {0.1, 0.1, 1} local CT_VIOLET = {0.79, 0.3, 0.85} local CT_GOLD = {1, 0.82, 0}
-- Colour · gate · flags · the message types that share them. `always` is the `show` an -- ungated type is born with; `jitter` is `isStaggered`; `gate` is `var`. local combatTextSpec = { -- Always on. Only the master toggle takes these away. {colour = CT_RED, always = 1, jitter = 1, types = {"DAMAGE"}}, {colour = CT_RED, always = 1, types = {"DAMAGE_CRIT"}}, {colour = CT_VIOLET, always = 1, types = {"SPELL_DAMAGE"}}, {colour = CT_WHITE, always = 1, types = {"SPLIT_DAMAGE"}}, {colour = CT_GREEN, always = 1, types = {"HEAL", "HEAL_CRIT", "PERIODIC_HEAL", "SPELL_CAST"}},
-- Never on by themselves: no `always`, no gate, so `show` is nil and stays nil. They -- carry a colour so that anything which does switch one on has one ready. {colour = CT_WHITE, types = {"INTERRUPT", "ENCHANTMENT_ADDED", "ENCHANTMENT_REMOVED", "DISPEL_FAILED", "SPELL_CAST_START", "SPELL_DISPELLED", "DAMAGE_SHIELD", "EXTRA_ATTACKS"}},
-- "Show dodge/parry/miss": swings that went nowhere, melee in red and spells in white. -- The melee whiffs jitter because several can land in the same instant. {colour = CT_RED, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_DODGE_PARRY_MISS", jitter = 1, types = {"MISS", "DODGE", "PARRY", "EVADE"}}, {colour = CT_RED, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_DODGE_PARRY_MISS", types = {"IMMUNE", "DEFLECT"}}, {colour = CT_WHITE, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_DODGE_PARRY_MISS", types = {"SPELL_MISSED", "SPELL_DODGED", "SPELL_PARRIED", "SPELL_EVADED", "SPELL_IMMUNE", "SPELL_DEFLECTED", "SPELL_REFLECTED"}},
-- "Show resistances": a hit that landed but was partly eaten. {colour = CT_RED, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_RESISTANCES", types = {"BLOCK", "ABSORB", "RESIST", "PROC_RESISTED"}}, {colour = CT_WHITE, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_RESISTANCES", types = {"SPELL_BLOCKED"}}, {colour = CT_VIOLET, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_RESISTANCES", types = {"SPELL_ABSORBED", "SPELL_RESISTED"}},
-- The aura pair — what landed, and what wore off — each split by whose side it helps. {colour = CT_GREEN, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_AURAS", types = {"AURA_START"}}, {colour = CT_RED, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_AURAS", types = {"AURA_START_HARMFUL"}}, {colour = CT_GREEN, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_AURA_FADE", types = {"AURA_END"}}, {colour = CT_RED, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_AURA_FADE", types = {"AURA_END_HARMFUL"}},
-- Resources and standing: everything you gained rather than took. {colour = CT_BLUE, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_MANA", types = {"MANA", "RAGE", "FOCUS", "ENERGY"}}, {colour = CT_BLUE, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_COMBO_POINTS", types = {"COMBO_POINTS"}}, {colour = CT_BLUE, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_REPUTATION", types = {"FACTION"}}, {colour = CT_BLUE, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_HONOR_GAINED", types = {"HONOR_GAINED"}},
-- The state warnings, each on its own switch. {colour = CT_RED, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_LOW_HEALTH_MANA", types = {"HEALTH_LOW", "MANA_LOW"}}, {colour = CT_RED, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_COMBAT_STATE", types = {"ENTERING_COMBAT", "LEAVING_COMBAT"}}, {colour = CT_GOLD, gate = "COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_REACTIVES", types = {"SPELL_ACTIVE"}}, }
COMBAT_TEXT_TYPE_INFO = {} for i = 1, getn(combatTextSpec) do local row = combatTextSpec[i] for j = 1, getn(row.types) do COMBAT_TEXT_TYPE_INFO[row.types[j]] = { r = row.colour[1], g = row.colour[2], b = row.colour[3], show = row.always, isStaggered = row.jitter, var = row.gate, } end end
-- A latched low-resource warning. The line prints on the crossing INTO the danger band and -- not again until the bar has climbed back out of it — otherwise every tick of a fight -- spent under 20% would print another one. `flag` names the field on the CombatText frame -- that remembers we already warned; `low` is the caller's verdict, because "low" is not -- the same question for the two bars (mana additionally requires the bar to BE mana: a -- rage or energy user is never low on mana). Returns the message type to print, or nil. local function CombatText_LowResourceWarning(flag, low, messageType) if not low then CombatText[flag] = nil return nil end if CombatText[flag] then return nil end CombatText[flag] = 1 return messageType end
-- The engine events whose entire meaning is "print this message type". Everything else -- either carries its own type in arg1 (COMBAT_TEXT_UPDATE) or IS its own type. local combatTextStateMessage = { PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED = "ENTERING_COMBAT", PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED = "LEAVING_COMBAT", }
function CombatText_OnLoad() CombatText_UpdateDisplayedMessages() CombatText.previousMana = {} end
function CombatText_OnEvent(event) -- What we are about to print: the type (which picks the colour and the gating), the -- payload it formats from, the finished line, and the optional "crit" presentation. local messageType, message local data = arg2 local displayType
if event == "UNIT_HEALTH" then if arg1 == "player" then local low = UnitHealth("player") / UnitHealthMax("player") <= COMBAT_TEXT_LOW_HEALTH_THRESHOLD messageType = CombatText_LowResourceWarning("lowHealth", low, "HEALTH_LOW") end if not messageType then return end elseif event == "UNIT_POWER_UPDATE" then -- Spec: UNIT_MANA + UnitMana/UnitManaMax (header deviation — the Era surface). -- Power type 0 is mana; the same event also carries rage, focus and energy, none -- of which has a low warning. local mana = UnitMana("player") local powerType = UnitPowerType("player") if arg1 == "player" then local low = mana / UnitManaMax("player") <= COMBAT_TEXT_LOW_MANA_THRESHOLD and powerType == 0 messageType = CombatText_LowResourceWarning("lowMana", low, "MANA_LOW") end if not messageType then return end elseif event == "PLAYER_COMBO_POINTS" then -- The count itself is the payload, and a full bar is worth a crit-sized line. -- Spending them fires this too, with nothing left to announce. data = GetComboPoints() if data <= 0 then return end messageType = "COMBO_POINTS" if data == MAX_COMBO_POINTS then displayType = "crit" end elseif event == "COMBAT_TEXT_UPDATE" then messageType = arg1 else messageType = combatTextStateMessage[event] or event end
-- The type decides the colour and whether this is printed at all. An unknown type -- is white and, having no `show`, prints nothing — which is how a message type we do -- not know about stays silent instead of erroring. local info = COMBAT_TEXT_TYPE_INFO[messageType] if not info then info = {r = 1, g = 1, b = 1} end if not info.show then return end
local isStaggered = info.isStaggered if messageType == "" then message = nil elseif messageType == "DAMAGE_CRIT" then displayType = "crit" message = "-" .. data elseif messageType == "DAMAGE" or messageType == "SPELL_DAMAGE" then message = "-" .. data elseif messageType == "SPELL_CAST" or messageType == "AURA_START" or messageType == "AURA_START_HARMFUL" then message = "<" .. data .. ">" elseif messageType == "AURA_END" or messageType == "AURA_END_HARMFUL" then message = format(AURA_END, data) elseif messageType == "HEAL" or messageType == "PERIODIC_HEAL" then if COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_FRIENDLY_NAMES == "1" and messageType == "HEAL" and UnitName("player") ~= data then message = "+" .. arg3 .. " [" .. data .. "]" else message = "+" .. arg3 end elseif messageType == "HEAL_CRIT" then displayType = "crit" if COMBAT_TEXT_SHOW_FRIENDLY_NAMES == "1" and UnitName("player") ~= data then message = "+" .. arg3 .. " [" .. data .. "]" else message = "+" .. arg3 end elseif messageType == "MANA" then if tonumber(data) > 0 then data = "+" .. data end message = data .. " " .. MANA elseif messageType == "RAGE" then message = "+" .. data .. " " .. RAGE elseif messageType == "FOCUS" then message = "+" .. data .. " " .. FOCUS elseif messageType == "ENERGY" then message = "+" .. data .. " " .. ENERGY elseif messageType == "FACTION" then if tonumber(arg3) > 0 then arg3 = "+" .. arg3 end message = "(" .. data .. " " .. arg3 .. ")" elseif messageType == "BLOCK" then if arg3 then message = data .. " " .. format(BLOCK_TRAILER, arg3) else message = BLOCK end elseif messageType == "ABSORB" then if arg3 then message = arg2 .. " " .. format(ABSORB_TRAILER, arg3) else message = ABSORB end elseif messageType == "RESIST" or messageType == "SPELL_RESISTED" then if arg3 then message = data .. " " .. format(RESIST_TRAILER, arg3) else message = RESIST end elseif messageType == "HONOR_GAINED" then if tonumber(data) > 0 then data = "+" .. data end message = format(COMBAT_TEXT_HONOR_GAINED, data) elseif messageType == "SPELL_ACTIVE" then displayType = "crit" message = "<" .. data .. ">" elseif messageType == "COMBO_POINTS" then message = data .. " Combo Points" else message = getglobal(messageType) if not message then message = getglobal("COMBAT_TEXT_" .. messageType) end end
-- A branch that produced no line (the empty type, or a global-string lookup that -- came back nil) simply prints nothing. if message then CombatText_AddMessage(message, COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLL_FUNCTION, info.r, info.g, info.b, displayType, isStaggered) end end
function CombatText_OnUpdate(elapsed) -- Backwards, so the removal inside the body can't skip a neighbor (the ref's 5.0 -- `for in` + tremove tolerated it; a 5.1 index loop must not). for i = getn(COMBAT_TEXT_TO_ANIMATE), 1, -1 do local value = COMBAT_TEXT_TO_ANIMATE[i] if value.scrollTime >= COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLLSPEED then CombatText_RemoveMessage(value) else value.scrollTime = value.scrollTime + elapsed local xPos, yPos = value.scrollFunction(value) value.yPos = yPos value:SetPoint("TOP", UIParent, "BOTTOM", xPos, yPos) if value.scrollTime >= COMBAT_TEXT_FADEOUT_TIME then local alpha = 1 - ((value.scrollTime - COMBAT_TEXT_FADEOUT_TIME) / (COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLLSPEED - COMBAT_TEXT_FADEOUT_TIME)) value:SetAlpha(max(alpha, 0)) end -- The crit pop: up to the maximum inside the scale window, back down by the -- shrink time, then it stops being a crit and holds its size. if value.isCrit then if value.scrollTime <= COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_SCALE_TIME then value:SetTextHeight(floor(COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_MINHEIGHT + ((COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_MAXHEIGHT - COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_MINHEIGHT) * value.scrollTime / COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_SCALE_TIME))) elseif value.scrollTime <= COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_SHRINKTIME then value:SetTextHeight(floor(COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_MAXHEIGHT - ((COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_MAXHEIGHT - COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_MINHEIGHT) * (value.scrollTime - COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_SCALE_TIME) / (COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_SHRINKTIME - COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_SCALE_TIME)))) else value.isCrit = nil end end end end end
-- A string that is not in flight: invisible, hidden, and back on the seat so the next -- caller measures it from a known place. Both ways out of the animation list end here. local function CombatText_ParkString(string) string:SetAlpha(0) string:Hide() string:SetPoint("TOP", UIParent, "BOTTOM", COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.startX, COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.startY) end
function CombatText_AddMessage(message, scrollFunction, r, g, b, displayType, isStaggered) local string, noStringsAvailable = CombatText_GetAvailableString() if noStringsAvailable then return end
string:SetText(message) string:SetTextColor(r, g, b) string.scrollTime = 0
-- Where the line is seated. `flow` is the direction the STACK grows — back down the -- way the run came, so -1 when the mode floats upward and +1 when it floats down — -- and having it as a number is what lets one walk serve both modes. Start at the -- string's own parked edge, then push clear of every line already in flight by one -- 16-unit line plus COMBAT_TEXT_SPACING; if that has carried the stack further than -- COMBAT_TEXT_MAX_OFFSET from the seat, start the column over at the parked edge -- instead of marching off the screen. (`GetBottom`/`GetTop` are nil before the first -- layout resolve — the parked seat stands in; identical after frame 1.) local flow, parkedY if COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.startY < COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.endY then flow = -1 parkedY = string:GetBottom() else flow = 1 parkedY = string:GetTop() end parkedY = parkedY or COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.startY
local seatY = parkedY for i = 1, getn(COMBAT_TEXT_TO_ANIMATE) do local clearOf = COMBAT_TEXT_TO_ANIMATE[i].yPos + flow * (16 + COMBAT_TEXT_SPACING) if (clearOf - seatY) * flow >= 0 then seatY = clearOf end end if (seatY - COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.startY) * flow > COMBAT_TEXT_MAX_OFFSET then seatY = parkedY end
-- Everything `displayType` decides, in one place. A crit pops through its own scale -- envelope and always takes the straight scroll (an arc would fight the pop); a crit or -- a sticky ends where it began, so it holds the seat instead of travelling; anything -- else takes the caller's scroll and runs the whole way. if displayType == "crit" then string.scrollFunction = CombatText_StandardScroll string.isCrit = 1 string.endY = COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.startY string:SetTextHeight(COMBAT_TEXT_CRIT_MINHEIGHT) else string.scrollFunction = scrollFunction string:SetTextHeight(COMBAT_TEXT_HEIGHT) if displayType == "sticky" then string.endY = COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.startY else string.endY = COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.endY end end
-- The fountain arcs alternate sides, so consecutive lines do not trace one path. if CombatText.xDir == 1 then CombatText.xDir = -1 else CombatText.xDir = 1 end string.xDir = CombatText.xDir
-- Staggered types jitter up to half COMBAT_TEXT_STAGGER_RANGE either side of centre. string.startX = COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.startX if isStaggered then string.startX = string.startX + random(0, COMBAT_TEXT_STAGGER_RANGE) - COMBAT_TEXT_STAGGER_RANGE / 2 end
string.startY = seatY string.yPos = seatY string:SetPoint("TOP", UIParent, "BOTTOM", string.startX, seatY) string:SetAlpha(1) string:Show() tinsert(COMBAT_TEXT_TO_ANIMATE, string) end
function CombatText_RemoveMessage(string) for i = 1, getn(COMBAT_TEXT_TO_ANIMATE) do if COMBAT_TEXT_TO_ANIMATE[i] == string then tremove(COMBAT_TEXT_TO_ANIMATE, i) CombatText_ParkString(string) break end end end
function CombatText_GetAvailableString() local string for i = 1, NUM_COMBAT_TEXT_LINES do string = getglobal("CombatText" .. i) if not string:IsShown() then return string end end return CombatText_GetOldestString(), 1 end
function CombatText_GetOldestString() local oldestString = COMBAT_TEXT_TO_ANIMATE[1] CombatText_RemoveMessage(oldestString) return oldestString end
function CombatText_ClearAnimationList() COMBAT_TEXT_TO_ANIMATE = {} for i = 1, NUM_COMBAT_TEXT_LINES do CombatText_ParkString(getglobal("CombatText" .. i)) end end
function CombatText_UpdateDisplayedMessages() -- The master toggle is enforced at the source: with the feature off we stop -- listening entirely rather than filtering every message as it arrives. if SHOW_COMBAT_TEXT == "0" then CombatText:UnregisterEvent("COMBAT_TEXT_UPDATE") CombatText:UnregisterEvent("UNIT_HEALTH") CombatText:UnregisterEvent("UNIT_POWER_UPDATE") CombatText:UnregisterEvent("PLAYER_COMBO_POINTS") CombatText:UnregisterEvent("PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED") CombatText:UnregisterEvent("PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED") return else CombatText:RegisterEvent("COMBAT_TEXT_UPDATE") CombatText:RegisterEvent("UNIT_HEALTH") CombatText:RegisterEvent("UNIT_POWER_UPDATE") CombatText:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_COMBO_POINTS") CombatText:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED") CombatText:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED") end -- Re-read every gated type's option into its `show`. This is the only writer of -- `show` for a type that carries a `var`, so it runs on every option change. for messageType, value in pairs(COMBAT_TEXT_TYPE_INFO) do if value.var then if getglobal(value.var) == "1" then value.show = 1 else value.show = nil end end end -- The engine's UI space is the 768-virtual coordinate system itself (decision -- 0582), so the ref constants stand verbatim (0581's px shim retired). The ref's -- uiScale-cvar division joins when a cvar system exists. local uiScale = 1 -- The float mode picks the path and the run: modes 1 and 3 rise to 609 (3 on an -- arc), mode 2 falls to 159. All three start at the same seat. if COMBAT_TEXT_FLOAT_MODE == "1" then COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLL_FUNCTION = CombatText_StandardScroll COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS = { startX = 0, startY = 384 / uiScale, endX = 0, endY = 609 / uiScale } elseif COMBAT_TEXT_FLOAT_MODE == "2" then COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLL_FUNCTION = CombatText_StandardScroll COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS = { startX = 0, startY = 384 / uiScale, endX = 0, endY = 159 / uiScale } else COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLL_FUNCTION = CombatText_FountainScroll COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS = { startX = 0, startY = 384 / uiScale, endX = 0, endY = 609 / uiScale } end CombatText_ClearAnimationList() end
function CombatText_StandardScroll(value) local xPos = value.startX + ((COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.endX - COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.startX) * value.scrollTime / COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLLSPEED) local yPos = value.startY + ((value.endY - COMBAT_TEXT_LOCATIONS.startY) * value.scrollTime / COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLLSPEED) return xPos, yPos end
function CombatText_FountainScroll(value) local radius = 150 local xPos = value.xDir * (value.startX + radius * cos(90 * value.scrollTime / COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLLSPEED)) - value.xDir * radius local yPos = value.startY + radius * sin(90 * value.scrollTime / COMBAT_TEXT_SCROLLSPEED) return xPos, yPos end
